title: Stale DNS: haven.reviewcommit.com points at a terminated EC2 instance
description:
Found 2026-11-22 while fixing the interop tools' defaults.

  haven.reviewcommit.com  A  18.116.164.157  -> connection fails (curl 000)

The A record outlived the EC2 instance it named. mimid-1wgh.46.20.1's
notes say "The old hosts are terminated", so this is a leftover from
that teardown, the same class as the stale records deleted earlier in
the week.

Two reasons to remove it rather than leave it:

1. It is worse than no record. A name that resolves but never answers
   produces a hang and a timeout; NXDOMAIN fails immediately and says
   why. It cost time here: it was mimid-chat's default --hub, so the
   tool appeared to work and then stalled.
2. 18.116.164.157 is an AWS address that is no longer ours. It will be
   reassigned to someone else, and a record of Mark's would then point
   at a stranger's host. That is a dangling-DNS takeover, and the name
   "haven" makes it worse: anything still pointing there would be
   talking to whoever holds the address next.

ACTION: delete the A record for haven.reviewcommit.com at Epik. From
joumon, over IPv4 (curl -4: the signature is registered to joumon's v4
and it egresses v6 by default), key from rbw, and the v2 endpoint --
never v1 SetHostRecords, which replaces the whole record set.

While there, check for other records left from the terminated hosts.
The zone listing of 2026-11-22 also showed www, social, irc, mimi and
mimid1._mimi.mimi; mimi and irc are live, and mimid.reviewcommit.com
correctly has no record at all.

Not done in this session: it is a destructive change to live DNS and
Mark had not asked for it.
notes: DONE 2026-11-22, Mark asked for it. Confirmed dead first from joumon: TCP 443, 8443 and 22 all closed/filtered, HTTPS 000. Deleted by record id 41f7a65d245b3041a8f9d11674ce9d4a via the Epik v2 DELETE from joumon over IPv4; answer code 1000. Verified by diffing full zone listings taken before and after: 18 records -> 17, exactly one removed (haven A 18.116.164.157), zero changed, zero added. Survivors intact, including mimid1._mimi.mimi TXT (the provider key), mimi A/AAAA, the MX, SPF and DKIM records and the CAA records. Both authoritative nameservers now return nothing for haven.reviewcommit.com, and mimi.reviewcommit.com still answers 200. No other records from the terminated hosts remain: mimid.reviewcommit.com already had none.
